entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery identity input has an unnamed column
entries.rationale: both callers pass a lowering-owned sample relation into the subquery RangeWindow boundary. Such relations either already declare the requested timestamp role (the early return) or expose a closed, fully named projection that this helper re-roles. An unnamed output is malformed internal plan IR, not a PromQL input rejection.

guard: past returning if column, ok := row.Find(chplan.RoleTimestamp); ok && column.Name == timestamp

Selector, call, arithmetic, and aggregate lowerers close that public sample shape before this helper runs; an open schema here is malformed internal plan IR rather than a query-dependent PromQL rejection.

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: subquery identity input is missing timestamp column %q
entries.rationale: both callers request a timestamp name fixed by the lowering contract: the configured metrics timestamp for an identity wrapper or anchor_ts for an outer reducer. Their lowering-owned inputs either already carry that role or project the named column; its absence is malformed internal plan IR, not a supported user query that Prometheus accepts and Cerberus rejects.
